**Yes. If Monzo goes bust, the UK’s Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS) protects up to £120,000 per person in eligible cash deposits held with Monzo Bank.** Monzo is a UK-authorised bank, so your deposits have the same protection as they would at a UK high-street bank. In most cases, the FSCS pays you back automatically within seven working days; you don’t need to make a claim. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/faq?utm_source=openai))

The key point is that the limit is **per person, not per account**. Add together your Monzo current account, regular Pots, savings held directly with Monzo, and your share of any joint account. A two-person joint account can have up to £240,000 protected in total, but each person’s share counts towards their own £120,000 limit. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/legal/files/fscs-information/fscs-information-2.0.pdf?utm_source=openai))

If your total is above £120,000, you can keep the excess protected by holding it at another UK-authorised bank **with a separate banking licence**. There’s also an exception for certain temporary balances: for example, proceeds from selling your main home may be protected up to £1.4 million for six months. ([protected.fscs.org.uk](https://protected.fscs.org.uk/making-a-claim/customer-info/banking-licences/?utm_source=openai))
